thread_text:
alex: Thinking out loud — propose a 'roulette' quantile-driven synthetic generator for shaping long-tail latency. idea: pick target quantiles (p50,p90,p99,p999) and stitch short ramps that push those quantiles with controlled bursts so we can exercise kernel-switch and KV-warm paths without long long runs.

maria: short version: we want knobs to force different kernel selection decisions and KV cache cold/warm transitions right? :+1:

alex: exactly. two concrete knobs: 1) quantile targets array (example below), 2) burst phase pattern (e.g., metronome vs jittered clusters). generator will emit sequences like: p90-heavy ramp -> short cooldown -> p999 spike -> steady p50.

cheng: can you paste a sample config? makes it easier to reason about warmups and batching buckets.

alex: sure — draft config:

```json
{
  "seed": 42,
  "quantile_targets": [0.5, 0.9, 0.99, 0.999],
  "phase_sequence": [
    {"mode":"ramp","q":0.9,"duration_ms":30000,"qps":200},
    {"mode":"burst","q":0.999,"duration_ms":5000,"peak_qps":1200},
    {"mode":"steady","q":0.5,"duration_ms":60000,"qps":50}
  ],
  "kv_warm_policy": "staggered",
  "sticky_kernel": false
}
```

alex: notes: `kv_warm_policy: staggered` means we intentionally interleave large-prefill requests on a subset of connection shards to create partial cache heating and observe miss patterns. `sticky_kernel` toggles forcing runtime to stick to selected kernels across phase boundaries for A/B.

bench-bot: run 2178909999 started (small-preview). config hash abc123. quick summary: p50=18ms p90=74ms p99=215ms p999=842ms. observed two kernel switches during the p999 spike (kernels: fast-attn->fallback-unrolled).

maria: those numbers look reasonable. do we have per-request tags to separate warmup-prefill vs steady traffic in traces? otherwise the KV misses will pollute the steady quantiles.

alex: yes — generator will tag requests: {"phase":"ramp","prefill":true/false,"seed_idx":N}. we keep a small span attribute so console can filter.

cheng: couple of concerns: 1) batching heuristics interact badly with tiny jittered bursts — the runtime might coalesce across shards and hide intended pressure. we should add a `batch_inhibit` window option for the generator to force near-empty batches on some percentage of requests. 2) ensure payload diversity (len tokens, prompt shapes) so kernel selection isn't always same path.

alex: good call. will add `batch_inhibit_pct` and a token-length distribution sampler.

tim: for apples-to-apples, we need a deterministic baseline run: same seed, `sticky_kernel=true`, `kv_warm_policy=full_prefill`, and no `batch_inhibit`. then compare to roulette run. use `--artifact-tag=roulette-vs-baseline` so CI picks it up.

bench-bot: quick diff artifact created: baseline vs roulette (link: https://ci.redwood/test/2178909999). baseline p999=540ms, roulette p999=842ms, kernel-switch-count +2, avg tokens/req same.

sara: does the harness support replaying captured real traffic sequences? i.e., feed a day's trace but apply quantile-targeted reshaping on top? would help sanity-check that synthetic isn't creating pathological switching that never happens in production.

alex: plan: 1) implement generator flags (seed, quantile_targets, phase_sequence, batch_inhibit_pct, payload_dist, kv_warm_policy, sticky_kernel), 2) add trace-replay overlay mode, 3) add small CLI that emits phase markers to tracing and sets request attributes. target PR by EOD Fri.

maria: +1. also add an exporter metric for 'kernel_switch_events' and 'kv_miss_window_rate' so we can correlate spikes to internal events.

alex: will do. thanks team — I'll post PR link when ready and schedule a short run during quiet hours. :rocket:
